title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock II

analysis.problem_summary: Find the maximum total profit from buying and selling a stock multiple times, holding at most one share at any time.
analysis.intuition: Since we can buy and sell on the same day, capturing any multi-day price increase (e.g., buying on day A and selling on day C) is mathematically identical to accumulating every consecutive daily price increase along that upward trend (A to B, then B to C). Therefore, we simply add up every positive price difference between consecutive days.
approach: Iterate through the price array starting from index 1 to the end.
For each day `i`, compare `prices[i]` with the previous day's price `prices[i - 1]`.
If `prices[i] > prices[i - 1]`, add the difference `prices[i] - prices[i - 1]` to `maxProfit`.
Return `maxProfit` after examining all consecutive price pairs.
analysis.why_it_works: Any profit over a strictly increasing sequence $p_1 \le p_2 \le \dots \le p_k$ equals $(p_k - p_1)$, which can be decomposed into $(p_2 - p_1) + (p_3 - p_2) + \dots + (p_k - p_{k-1})$. On decreasing steps, we abstain from trading (0 profit contribution). Summing all positive single-day differences captures the global optimal profit without needing explicit state management.
analysis.key_takeaway: When unlimited transactions are permitted without transaction fees, maximizing total profit reduces to collecting every positive single-step gradient.
analysis.time_explanation: The algorithm iterates through the `prices` array of size $n$ exactly once, performing constant-time comparisons and additions at each step.
analysis.space_explanation: Only a single variable (`maxProfit`) is used to maintain the running total profit, requiring $O(1)$ extra space.
